correctness.rationale: In each indexed prism column a selected rung, top rail or bottom rail excludes all other edges starting in the same or a neighboring column. At directed separation two a starting rung allows every second type; a starting rail allows only the opposite rail. The wrap-around tests enforce both orientations when n=4, and for n=3 every pair of distinct columns is consecutive. Larger separations in both directions cannot give adjacent endpoints. The seven-state closed walks keep the first column fixed by the vertex labels, so trace counts indexed words, not rotation classes. Independently, the block for the allowed distance-two pairs in order R,T,B has rows (1,1,1),(0,0,1),(0,1,0). Eliminating the transit states gives, with d=zt², the determinant (1+d)[(1−t)(1−d)^2−zt³(3−d)], the claimed factorization. The formal logarithmic derivative gives the traces; the only excluded traces are 1 and 1+2z at lengths one and two. All-rung choices attain floor(n/2). At odd n, the sole gap of length three leaves an open chain of occupied types; there are n choices for the gap and n types of chains (all rungs or a first rail of either kind followed by forced alternation). At even n, each of two supports allows all rungs and allows two additional alternating rail assignments exactly when n/2 is even. Independent exact adjacency checks over 87,360 words for n=3..8 agreed, including 1+24z+148z²+176z³+6z⁴ at n=8. Frozen verify.py was inspected, not executed; it documents a separate finite check through order nine and extremal traces through order 44. The graph bijection, determinant identity, and gap proof, not either finite range, establish the theorem.

value.rationale: The prism is the natural periodic version of the classical open width-two problem. Closure changes the transfer modes that contribute to the all-size distribution, and changes the extremal structure sharply: quadratically many optima at odd n become only six or two at even n. This supplies exact benchmarks for a canonical cubic family rather than a few computed coefficients.
